title: The Princess and the Pea
description: A stormy night, a mysterious visitor, and twenty soft featherbeds test whether a visitor is truly royal.
subtitle: A stormy night, a mysterious visitor, and twenty soft featherbeds test whether a visitor is truly royal.

cover.alt: The young prince standing in a grand sunlit castle library, looking out of an arched window over distant hills.

scenes.title: The Search for a True Princess

blocks.html: Once upon a time there was a prince who wanted to marry a princess; but she would have to be a real princess.

blocks.alt: The young prince standing in a grand sunlit castle library, looking out of an arched window over distant hills
blocks.caption: The prince longed to find a real princess to share his life and kingdom.

blocks.html: He travelled all over the world to find one, but nowhere could he get what he wanted.
There were princesses enough, but it was difficult to find out whether they were real ones. There was always something about them that was not as it should be.

blocks.alt: The young prince on a noble white horse riding past faraway kingdoms and winding roads
blocks.caption: He rode through faraway lands, yet no one could prove they were truly royal.

blocks.html: So he came home again and was sad, for he would have liked very much to have a real princess.

blocks.alt: The dejected prince sitting with the kindly king and queen by the warm castle hearth
blocks.caption: The prince returned home with a heavy heart, despairing of ever finding true royalty.

blocks.html: One evening a terrible storm came on. There was thunder and lightning, and the rain poured down in torrents.

blocks.alt: Dark swirling storm clouds and lightning flashes over the castle towers
blocks.caption: A fierce autumn storm rolled over the kingdom with thunder, lightning, and pouring rain.

blocks.html: Suddenly a knocking was heard at the city gate.

blocks.alt: The heavy iron-studded city gate in the pouring rain with a glowing lantern
blocks.caption: Through the howl of the wind came an urgent knocking at the heavy town gate.

blocks.html: And the old king went to open it.

blocks.alt: The kindly elderly king holding a glowing lantern as he unbars the heavy gate to the stormy night
blocks.caption: The old king lifted his lantern into the stormy night to greet the traveller.

blocks.html: It was a princess standing out there in front of the gate. But, good gracious! What a sight the rain and the wind had made her look.
The water ran down from her hair and clothes; it ran down into the toes of her shoes and out again at the heels. And yet she said that she was a real princess.

blocks.alt: The shivering, dripping princess standing in the castle entrance hall in a drenched lavender gown
blocks.caption: Water ran from her soaked hair and shoes, yet she spoke with gentle princess dignity.

blocks.html: Well, we'll soon find that out, thought the old queen.

blocks.alt: The wise elderly queen smiling knowingly as she inspects a tiny green pea in her hand
blocks.caption: The wise old queen said nothing, but secretly devised a test of pure sensitivity.

blocks.html: She went into the bed-room, took all the bedding off the bedstead, and laid a pea on the bottom.

blocks.alt: Close-up of a small round green pea resting on the bare wooden slats of the four-poster bed
blocks.caption: Upon the bare wooden bedstead, the queen carefully laid one tiny, hard round pea.

blocks.html: Then she took twenty mattresses and laid them on the pea.

blocks.alt: Maidservants and the queen piling twenty colorful, thick mattresses high upon the bed
blocks.caption: Twenty thick, soft mattresses were piled atop the little pea, one above another.

blocks.html: And then twenty eider-down beds on top of the mattresses.

blocks.alt: Fluffy eider-down featherbeds and quilts towering up toward the high stone ceiling
blocks.caption: Twenty light and fluffy eider-down featherbeds were stacked above the mattresses.

blocks.html: On this the princess had to lie all night.

blocks.alt: The princess in a clean nightgown climbing a wooden ladder to reach the towering bed
blocks.caption: Using a tall wooden ladder, the weary guest climbed high into the mountain of bedding.

blocks.html: In the morning she was asked how she had slept.

blocks.alt: The princess tossing and turning sleeplessly in the moonlight atop the towering bed
blocks.caption: All night long, the princess tossed and turned, unable to find rest on the strange bed.

blocks.html:
The Princess's Morning Reply

"Oh, very badly!" said she. "I have scarcely closed my eyes all night. Heaven only knows what was in the bed, but I was lying on something hard, so that I am black and blue all over my body. It's horrible!"
Now they knew that she was a real princess, because she had felt the pea right through the twenty mattresses and the twenty eider-down beds. Nobody but a real princess could be as sensitive as that.

blocks.alt: The royal family gathered around the breakfast table in delight as the princess explains her night
blocks.caption: Only someone of genuine royal delicacy could feel a tiny pea through forty layers of bedding!

blocks.html: So the prince took her for his wife, for now he knew that he had a real princess; and the pea was put in the museum, where it may still be seen, if no one has stolen it.
There, that is a true story.

blocks.alt: The joyful wedding of the prince and princess, and the pea preserved in a royal museum vitrine
blocks.caption: The prince found his true princess at last, and the famous pea was placed in the royal museum.

discussionHtml:
💡 Bedtime Discussion

What made the princess truly royal?

Hans Christian Andersen shows that true royalty is not about crown or riches, but genuine sensitivity, honesty, and grace under adversity.
